identity.title: Schema Registry
identity.subTitle: Part 1: In-server registry of encoding schemas
introduction: An encoding such as Avro or Apache Arrow does not carry its own type information on the wire. A message is a compact payload plus a fingerprint of the schema that produced it, and a decoder that does not already hold that schema cannot read the message at all. Something has to turn a fingerprint back into a schema document, and it has to do so for every producer a consumer might meet.

That something is a schema registry: a store of schema documents addressed by identity rather than by location, with the versioning and compatibility rules that let a producer evolve a schema without breaking the consumers already deployed against it. Registries of this shape are well established outside OPC UA, and the xRegistry specification gives them a common model and HTTP API.

This document defines the same registry inside an OPC UA Server. A Server exposes its schemas as part of its own address space, so a Client resolves a fingerprint with the Services it already uses — Browse, Read and Call — without a second protocol, a second endpoint or a second set of credentials.
